subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-call recap / next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@streamly.io>, Elena Vázquez <elena.vazquez@streamly.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-call recap / next steps

Hi Tom / Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to learn more about Streamly's real-time transcript use case and the constraints around live captioning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned on performance requirements: 

Priority SLOs we heard today:
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target <= 100 ms for 75% of live requests, p95 <= 200 ms. This is the top priority for UX.
- Streaming: server-sent events (SSE) preferred for browser client simplicity; WebSocket is acceptable as fallback.
- Chunk cadence: payloads should arrive in ~150-300 ms cadence (ideally ~200 ms) to keep captions feeling live.
- Throughput / concurrency: planning for baseline 2k req/s with bursts to 4k during peak events; expected sustained concurrency ~500 active streams.

Open questions / asks from Redwood to Streamly:
1) Can you share representative payload sizes and average prompt lengths (tokens)? This helps us size batching and KV cache behavior.
2) Please provide a short traffic profile (RPS over a typical day, and peak window) and an ideal test window (e.g., 1-minute, 5-minute peaks).
3) Any network constraints on the client side (e.g., mobile over 3G)?

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa and I will run a focused benchmark session with our streaming runtime (SSE + chunk cadence tuning). Target: reproduce a 1-minute peak with your sample payloads.
- You share sample payloads and an S3 link (or zipped attachment) -> we’ll run instrumentation with TTFT probes and per-chunk latency breakdown.
- Follow-up sync next week to review benchmark results and recommended config (batching, quantization, routing).

Attaching our measurement guidelines so you know exactly how we capture TTFT and chunk cadence (see redwood-ttft-measurement-guidelines.pdf).

If this looks right, can we schedule the benchmark run Tues/Wed next week?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

[attachment: redwood-ttft-measurement-guidelines.pdf]

From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@streamly.io>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Vázquez <elena.vazquez@streamly.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-call recap / next steps

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- TTFT target: our product team would like to aim for <= 80 ms median, p95 <= 150 ms if achievable, but we can accept the <=100 ms / p95<=200 ms you noted as a baseline for procurement.
- Streaming protocol: SSE preferred for web clients; we'll accept WebSocket for mobile where SSE support varies.
- Chunk cadence: 150-250 ms preferred — 200 ms is our target.
- Throughput/Concurrency: baseline 2k req/s is correct; during a big event we can see sustained 3.5k for ~10 minutes.

I've uploaded a zipped set of ~500 sample prompts (varied lengths) to our S3 bucket: s3://streamly-shared/sample-payloads/streamly_payloads_v1.zip — it contains metadata with token counts. Also adding a short CSV with traffic profile.

We can do the benchmark run on Wednesday (6/17) morning Pacific. Please confirm a 60–90 min slot.

—Tom
Tom Harris
Head of Product, Streamly Inc.
tharris@streamly.io

[attachment: streamly-sample-payloads.zip]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@streamly.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-call recap / next steps

Tom — perfect, thanks for the S3 link and the more aggressive TTFT target (we’ll treat <=80 ms median as stretch goal).

We’ll do the following before Wed 6/17 run: 
- Marissa will provision an isolated benchmark harness that mirrors the SSE path and pins model variants for consistent comparison.
- We’ll instrument TTFT at the edge (connection accept -> first chunk sent) and at the model runtime (request in -> token emit).
- Please confirm an example client scenario (browser vs mobile) so we can reproduce client-side latency characteristics.

Proposed benchmarking goals for the session:
1) Measure TTFT distribution (median, p75, p95) under your 1-minute peak (3.5k sustained) and normal baseline (2k).
2) Measure per-chunk latency and chunk cadence distribution to validate 200 ms target.
3) Verify SSE vs WebSocket behavior; collect socket-level metrics (reconnects, dropped chunks).

I’ll put a calendar invite for Wed 6/17 09:00 PT — sending now.

Aditya

---Forwarded-by Marissa for scheduling---
